source_access: Primary formulas opened directly through web tools; no downloaded-byte digest claimed.
strongest_comparator: The retained flat tower has a fixed p^4 logarithmic normal symbol and an O(p^3) remainder. The geodesic-seam estimates concern compact cores or form closures, without a moving-cut boundary representative. The cubic remainder bound is insufficient for the cusp generated by nonzero finite-cut normal derivatives.
hardest_step: Keep the boundary derivative contact in the homogeneous continuation and local logarithm, then control the moving-cut form through the Mellin energy, a Carleman reflection term and a boundary distribution paired against H1 functions. Improve the entire flat tower remainder to O(p^2 log p) before using a nonsmooth even extension.
new_consequence: The specified compensated full flat geodesic angular-tower model has a finite translated-logarithmic weak cutoff limit on its stated form domain and cannot supply the persistent oscillatory cancellation required by the previous coupled trace result.
remaining_quantum_gap: A finite-cut actual-minus-model comparison and identification of the actual energy space with the normal form domain are unproved. Curvature, thermal/global effects, the potential and actual second mass vertex must remain in that comparison.
regulator_contract: No physical averaging prescription or original finite counterterm is changed. The homogeneous analytic continuation defines the normal representative; agreement of its critical a4 coefficient alone is not a proof that it equals the full physical determinant.
verification_scope: Symbolic heat/contact normalization and trapezoid constants; independent subtracted Fourier and finite-part integrals; Mellin kernels and cut-profile limits; full angular digamma sums checked against convergent sums with explicit tail enclosures. Continuum results remain ordinary arguments, not numerical certification of a physical solution.
